L00001: # Spider: A Large-Scale Human-Labeled Dataset for Complex and Cross-Domain Semantic Parsing and Text-to-SQL Task
L00002: 
L00003: Spider is a large human-labeled dataset for complex and cross-domain semantic parsing and text-to-SQL task (natural language interfaces for relational databases). It is released along with our EMNLP 2018 paper: [Spider: A Large-Scale Human-Labeled Dataset for Complex and Cross-Domain Semantic Parsing and Text-to-SQL Task](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.08887). This repo contains all code for evaluation, preprocessing, and all baselines used in our paper. Please refer to [the task site](https://yale-lily.github.io/spider) for more general introduction and the leaderboard.
L00004: 
L00005: :+1: `03/20/2022`: **We open-sourced a simple but SOTA model (just T5) for the task! Please check out our code in the [UnifiedSKG repo](https://github.com/hkunlp/unifiedskg)!!**
L00006: 
L00007: ### Changelog
L00008: -`11/15/2020` We will use [Test Suite Accuracy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.02840) as our official evaluation metric for Spider, SParC, and CoSQL. Please find the evaluation code from [here](https://github.com/taoyds/test-suite-sql-eval).
L00009: - `08/03/2020` Corrected `column_name` and `column_name_original` mismatches in 2 dbs (`scholar` and `formula_1`) in `tables.json`, and reparsed SQL queries (this only affects some models (e.g. RATSQL) which use our parsed SQL as the SQL input). Please download the Spider dataset from [the page](https://yale-lily.github.io/spider) again.
L00010: - `06/07/2020` We corrected some annotation errors and label mismatches (not errors) in Spider dev and test sets (~4% of dev examples updated, click [here](https://github.com/taoyds/spider/commit/25fcd85d9b6e94acaeb5e9172deadeefeed83f5e#diff-18b0a730a7b0d29b0a78a5070d971d49) for more details). Please download the Spider dataset from [the page](https://yale-lily.github.io/spider) again.
L00011: - `01/16/2020` For value prediction (in order to compute the execution accuracy), your model should be able to 1) copy from the question inputs, 2) retrieve from the database content (database content is available), or 3) generate numbers (e.g. 3 in "LIMIT 3").
L00012: - `1/14/2019` The submission toturial is ready! Please follow it to get your results on the unreleased test data.
L00013: - `12/17/2018` We updated 7 sqlite database files. Please download the Spider data from the official website again. Please refer to [the issue 14](https://github.com/taoyds/spider/issues/14) for more details.
L00014: - `10/25/2018`: evaluation script is updated so that the table in `count(*)`cases will be evaluated as well. Please check out [the issue 5](https://github.com/taoyds/spider/issues/5) for more info. Results of all baselines and [syntaxSQL](https://github.com/taoyds/syntaxSQL) on the papers are updated as well.
L00015: - `10/25/2018`: to get the latest SQL parsing results (a few small bugs fixed), please use `preprocess/parse_raw_json.py` to update. Please refer to [the issue 3](https://github.com/taoyds/spider/issues/3) for more details.
L00016: 
L00017: ### Citation
L00018:

L00031: 
L00032: ### Installation
L00033: 
L00034: `evaluation.py` and `process_sql.py` are written in Python 3. Enviroment setup for each baseline is in README under each baseline directory.
L00035: 
L00036: 
L00037: ### Data Content and Format
L00038: 
L00039: #### Question, SQL, and Parsed SQL
L00040: 
L00041: Each file in`train.json` and `dev.json` contains the following fields:
L00042: - `question`: the natural language question
L00043: - `question_toks`: the natural language question tokens
L00044: - `db_id`: the database id to which this question is addressed.
L00045: - `query`: the SQL query corresponding to the question. 
L00046: - `query_toks`: the SQL query tokens corresponding to the question. 
L00047: - `sql`: parsed results of this SQL query using `process_sql.py`. Please refer to `parsed_sql_examples.sql` in the`preprocess` directory for the detailed documentation.
L00048: 
L00049: 
L00050: ```
L00051:  {
L00052:         "db_id": "world_1",
L00053:         "query": "SELECT avg(LifeExpectancy) FROM country WHERE Name NOT IN (SELECT T1.Name FROM country AS T1 JOIN countrylanguage AS T2 ON T1.Code  =  T2.CountryCode WHERE T2.Language  =  \"English\" AND T2.IsOfficial  =  \"T\")",
L00054:         "query_toks": ["SELECT", "avg", "(", "LifeExpectancy", ")", "FROM", ...],
L00055:         "question": "What is average life expectancy in the countries where English is not the official language?",
L00056:         "question_toks": ["What", "is", "average", "life", ...],
L00057:         "sql": {
L00058:             "except": null,

L00075:                     true,
L00076:                     ...

L00081:                                 [
L00082:                                     false,

L00085:                                     ...

L00105:

L00107: 
L00108: #### Tables
L00109: 
L00110: `tables.json` contains the following information for each database:
L00111: - `db_id`: database id
L00112: - `table_names_original`: original table names stored in the database.
L00113: - `table_names`: cleaned and normalized table names. We make sure the table names are meaningful. [to be changed]
L00114: - `column_names_original`: original column names stored in the database. Each column looks like: `[0, "id"]`. `0` is the index of table names in `table_names`, which is `city` in this case. `"id"` is the column name. 
L00115: - `column_names`: cleaned and normalized column names. We make sure the column names are meaningful. [to be changed]
L00116: - `column_types`: data type of each column
L00117: - `foreign_keys`: foreign keys in the database. `[3, 8]` means column indices in the `column_names`. These two columns are foreign keys of two different tables.
L00118: - `primary_keys`: primary keys in the database. Each number is the index of `column_names`.

L00204: 
L00205: 
L00206: #### Databases
L00207: 
L00208: All table contents are contained in corresponding SQLite3 database files.
L00209: 
L00210: 
L00211: ### Evaluation
L00212: 
L00213: Update 11/15/20: We will use [Test Suite Accuracy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.02840) as our official evaluation metric for Spider, SParC, and CoSQL. Please find the evaluation code from [here](https://github.com/taoyds/test-suite-sql-eval).
L00214: Our evaluation metrics include Component Matching, Exact Matching, and Execution Accuracy. For component and exact matching evaluation, instead of simply conducting string comparison between the predicted and gold SQL queries, we decompose each SQL into several clauses, and conduct set comparison in each SQL clause. 
L00215: 
L00216: For Execution Accuracy, our current models do not predict any value in SQL conditions so that we do not provide execution accuracies. However, we encourage you to provide it in the future submissions. For value prediction, you can assume that a list of gold values for each question is given. Your model has to fill them into the right slots in the SQL.
L00217: 
L00218: Please refer to [our paper]() and [this page](https://github.com/taoyds/spider/tree/master/evaluation) for more details and examples.
L00219: 
L00220: ```
L00221: python evaluation.py --gold [gold file] --pred [predicted file] --etype [evaluation type] --db [database dir] --table [table file]
L00222: 
L00223: arguments:
L00224:   [gold file]        gold.sql file where each line is `a gold SQL \t db_id`
L00225:   [predicted file]   predicted sql file where each line is a predicted SQL
L00226:   [evaluation type]  "match" for exact set matching score, "exec" for execution score, and "all" for both
L00227:   [database dir]     directory which contains sub-directories where each SQLite3 database is stored
L00228:   [table file]       table.json file which includes foreign key info of each database
L00229:   
L00230: ```

L00017: def tokenize_for_bleu_eval(code):
L00018:     code = re.sub(r'([^A-Za-z0-9_])', r' \1 ', code)
L00019:     code = re.sub(r'([a-z])([A-Z])', r'\1 \2', code)
L00020:     code = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', code)
L00021:     code = code.replace('"', '`')
L00022:     code = code.replace('\'', '`')
L00023:     tokens = [t for t in code.split(' ') if t]
L00024: 
L00025:     return tokens

L00028: def evaluate(model, dataset, verbose=True):
L00029:     if verbose:
L00030:         logging.info('evaluating [%s] dataset, [%d] examples' % (dataset.name, dataset.count))
L00031: 
L00032:     exact_match_ratio = 0.0
L00033: 
L00034:     for example in dataset.examples:
L00035:         logging.info('evaluating example [%d]' % example.eid)
L00036:         hyps, hyp_scores = model.decode(example, max_time_step=config.decode_max_time_step)
L00037:         gold_rules = example.rules
L00038: 
L00039:         if len(hyps) == 0:
L00040:             logging.warning('no decoding result for example [%d]!' % example.eid)
L00041:             continue
L00042: 
L00043:         best_hyp = hyps[0]
L00044:         predict_rules = [dataset.grammar.id_to_rule[rid] for rid in best_hyp]
L00045: 
L00046:         assert len(predict_rules) > 0 and len(gold_rules) > 0
L00047: 
L00048:         exact_match = sorted(gold_rules, key=lambda x: x.__repr__()) == sorted(predict_rules, key=lambda x: x.__repr__())
L00049:         if exact_match:
L00050:             exact_match_ratio += 1

L00053:         # r = len(predict_rules.intersection(gold_rules)) / len(gold_rules)
L00054: 
L00055:     exact_match_ratio /= dataset.count
L00056: 
L00057:     logging.info('exact_match_ratio = %f' % exact_match_ratio)
L00058: 
L00059:     return exact_match_ratio

L00033: def moses_multi_bleu(hypotheses, references, lowercase=False):
L00034:   """Calculate the bleu score for hypotheses and references
L00035:   using the MOSES ulti-bleu.perl script.
L00036: 
L00037:   Args:
L00038:     hypotheses: A numpy array of strings where each string is a single example.
L00039:     references: A numpy array of strings where each string is a single example.
L00040:     lowercase: If true, pass the "-lc" flag to the multi-bleu script
L00041: 
L00042:   Returns:
L00043:     The BLEU score as a float32 value.
L00044:   """
L00045: 
L00046:   if np.size(hypotheses) == 0:
L00047:     return np.float32(0.0)
L00048: 
L00049:   # Get MOSES multi-bleu script
L00050:   try:
L00051:     multi_bleu_path, _ = urllib.request.urlretrieve(
L00052:         "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moses-smt/mosesdecoder/"
L00053:         "master/scripts/generic/multi-bleu.perl")
L00054:     os.chmod(multi_bleu_path, 0o755)
L00055:   except: #pylint: disable=W0702
L00056:     tf.logging.info("Unable to fetch multi-bleu.perl script, using local.")
L00057:     metrics_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__))
L00058:     bin_dir = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(metrics_dir, "..", "..", "bin"))
L00059:     multi_bleu_path = os.path.join(bin_dir, "tools/multi-bleu.perl")
L00060: 
L00061:   # Dump hypotheses and references to tempfiles
L00062:   hypothesis_file = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile()
L00063:   hypothesis_file.write("\n".join(hypotheses).encode("utf-8"))
L00064:   hypothesis_file.write(b"\n")
L00065:   hypothesis_file.flush()
L00066:   reference_file = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile()
L00067:   reference_file.write("\n".join(references).encode("utf-8"))
L00068:   reference_file.write(b"\n")
L00069:   reference_file.flush()
L00070: 
L00071:   # Calculate BLEU using multi-bleu script
L00072:   with open(hypothesis_file.name, "r") as read_pred:
L00073:     bleu_cmd = [multi_bleu_path]
L00074:     if lowercase:
L00075:       bleu_cmd += ["-lc"]
L00076:     bleu_cmd += [reference_file.name]
L00077:     try:
L00078:       bleu_out = subprocess.check_output(
L00079:           bleu_cmd, stdin=read_pred, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
L00080:       bleu_out = bleu_out.decode("utf-8")
L00081:       bleu_score = re.search(r"BLEU = (.+?),", bleu_out).group(1)
L00082:       bleu_score = float(bleu_score)
L00083:     except subprocess.CalledProcessError as error:
L00084:       if error.output is not None:
L00085:         tf.logging.warning("multi-bleu.perl script returned non-zero exit code")
L00086:         tf.logging.warning(error.output)
L00087:       bleu_score = np.float32(0.0)
L00088: 
L00089:   # Close temp files
L00090:   hypothesis_file.close()
L00091:   reference_file.close()
L00092: 
L00093:   return np.float32(bleu_score)

L00032: def _get_ngrams(n, text):
L00033:   """Calcualtes n-grams.

L00035:   Args:
L00036:     n: which n-grams to calculate
L00037:     text: An array of tokens
L00038: 
L00039:   Returns:
L00040:     A set of n-grams
L00041:   """
L00042:   ngram_set = set()
L00043:   text_length = len(text)
L00044:   max_index_ngram_start = text_length - n
L00045:   for i in range(max_index_ngram_start + 1):
L00046:     ngram_set.add(tuple(text[i:i + n]))
L00047:   return ngram_set

L00050: def _split_into_words(sentences):
L00051:   """Splits multiple sentences into words and flattens the result"""
L00052:   return list(itertools.chain(*[_.split(" ") for _ in sentences]))
L00053: 
L00054: 
L00055: def _get_word_ngrams(n, sentences):
L00056:   """Calculates word n-grams for multiple sentences.
L00057:   """
L00058:   assert len(sentences) > 0
L00059:   assert n > 0
L00060: 
L00061:   words = _split_into_words(sentences)
L00062:   return _get_ngrams(n, words)

L00065: def _len_lcs(x, y):
L00066:   """
L00067:   Returns the length of the Longest Common Subsequence between sequences x
L00068:   and y.
L00069:   Source: http://www.algorithmist.com/index.php/Longest_Common_Subsequence
L00070: 
L00071:   Args:
L00072:     x: sequence of words
L00073:     y: sequence of words
L00074: 
L00075:   Returns
L00076:     integer: Length of LCS between x and y
L00077:   """
L00078:   table = _lcs(x, y)
L00079:   n, m = len(x), len(y)
L00080:   return table[n, m]
L00081: 
L00082: 
L00083: def _lcs(x, y):
L00084:   """
L00085:   Computes the length of the longest common subsequence (lcs) between two
L00086:   strings. The implementation below uses a DP programming algorithm and runs
L00087:   in O(nm) time where n = len(x) and m = len(y).
L00088:   Source: http://www.algorithmist.com/index.php/Longest_Common_Subsequence
L00089: 
L00090:   Args:
L00091:     x: collection of words
L00092:     y: collection of words
L00093: 
L00094:   Returns:
L00095:     Table of dictionary of coord and len lcs
L00096:   """
L00097:   n, m = len(x), len(y)
L00098:   table = dict()
L00099:   for i in range(n + 1):
L00100:     for j in range(m + 1):
L00101:       if i == 0 or j == 0:
L00102:         table[i, j] = 0
L00103:       elif x[i - 1] == y[j - 1]:
L00104:         table[i, j] = table[i - 1, j - 1] + 1
L00105:       else:
L00106:         table[i, j] = max(table[i - 1, j], table[i, j - 1])
L00107:   return table
L00108: 
L00109: 
L00110: def _recon_lcs(x, y):
L00111:   """
L00112:   Returns the Longest Subsequence between x and y.
L00113:   Source: http://www.algorithmist.com/index.php/Longest_Common_Subsequence
L00114: 
L00115:   Args:
L00116:     x: sequence of words
L00117:     y: sequence of words
L00118: 
L00119:   Returns:
L00120:     sequence: LCS of x and y
L00121:   """
L00122:   i, j = len(x), len(y)
L00123:   table = _lcs(x, y)
L00124: 
L00125:   def _recon(i, j):
L00126:     """private recon calculation"""
L00127:     if i == 0 or j == 0:
L00128:       return []
L00129:     elif x[i - 1] == y[j - 1]:
L00130:       return _recon(i - 1, j - 1) + [(x[i - 1], i)]
L00131:     elif table[i - 1, j] > table[i, j - 1]:
L00132:       return _recon(i - 1, j)
L00133:     else:
L00134:       return _recon(i, j - 1)
L00135: 
L00136:   recon_tuple = tuple(map(lambda x: x[0], _recon(i, j)))
L00137:   return recon_tuple

L00140: def rouge_n(evaluated_sentences, reference_sentences, n=2):
L00141:   """
L00142:   Computes ROUGE-N of two text collections of sentences.
L00143:   Sourece: http://research.microsoft.com/en-us/um/people/cyl/download/
L00144:   papers/rouge-working-note-v1.3.1.pdf
L00145: 
L00146:   Args:
L00147:     evaluated_sentences: The sentences that have been picked by the summarizer
L00148:     reference_sentences: The sentences from the referene set
L00149:     n: Size of ngram.  Defaults to 2.
L00150: 
L00151:   Returns:
L00152:     A tuple (f1, precision, recall) for ROUGE-N
L00153: 
L00154:   Raises:
L00155:     ValueError: raises exception if a param has len <= 0
L00156:   """
L00157:   if len(evaluated_sentences) <= 0 or len(reference_sentences) <= 0:
L00158:     raise ValueError("Collections must contain at least 1 sentence.")
L00159: 
L00160:   evaluated_ngrams = _get_word_ngrams(n, evaluated_sentences)
L00161:   reference_ngrams = _get_word_ngrams(n, reference_sentences)
L00162:   reference_count = len(reference_ngrams)
L00163:   evaluated_count = len(evaluated_ngrams)
L00164: 
L00165:   # Gets the overlapping ngrams between evaluated and reference
L00166:   overlapping_ngrams = evaluated_ngrams.intersection(reference_ngrams)
L00167:   overlapping_count = len(overlapping_ngrams)
L00168: 
L00169:   # Handle edge case. This isn't mathematically correct, but it's good enough
L00170:   if evaluated_count == 0:
L00171:     precision = 0.0
L00172:   else:
L00173:     precision = overlapping_count / evaluated_count
L00174: 
L00175:   if reference_count == 0:
L00176:     recall = 0.0
L00177:   else:
L00178:     recall = overlapping_count / reference_count
L00179: 
L00180:   f1_score = 2.0 * ((precision * recall) / (precision + recall + 1e-8))
L00181: 
L00182:   # return overlapping_count / reference_count
L00183:   return f1_score, precision, recall

L00186: def _f_p_r_lcs(llcs, m, n):
L00187:   """
L00188:   Computes the LCS-based F-measure score
L00189:   Source: http://research.microsoft.com/en-us/um/people/cyl/download/papers/
L00190:   rouge-working-note-v1.3.1.pdf
L00191: 
L00192:   Args:
L00193:     llcs: Length of LCS
L00194:     m: number of words in reference summary
L00195:     n: number of words in candidate summary
L00196: 
L00197:   Returns:
L00198:     Float. LCS-based F-measure score
L00199:   """
L00200:   r_lcs = llcs / m
L00201:   p_lcs = llcs / n
L00202:   beta = p_lcs / (r_lcs + 1e-12)
L00203:   num = (1 + (beta**2)) * r_lcs * p_lcs
L00204:   denom = r_lcs + ((beta**2) * p_lcs)
L00205:   f_lcs = num / (denom + 1e-12)
L00206:   return f_lcs, p_lcs, r_lcs
L00207:

L00209: def rouge_l_sentence_level(evaluated_sentences, reference_sentences):
L00210:   """
L00211:   Computes ROUGE-L (sentence level) of two text collections of sentences.
L00212:   http://research.microsoft.com/en-us/um/people/cyl/download/papers/
L00213:   rouge-working-note-v1.3.1.pdf
L00214: 
L00215:   Calculated according to:
L00216:   R_lcs = LCS(X,Y)/m
L00217:   P_lcs = LCS(X,Y)/n
L00218:   F_lcs = ((1 + beta^2)*R_lcs*P_lcs) / (R_lcs + (beta^2) * P_lcs)
L00219: 
L00220:   where:
L00221:   X = reference summary
L00222:   Y = Candidate summary
L00223:   m = length of reference summary
L00224:   n = length of candidate summary

L00226:   Args:
L00227:     evaluated_sentences: The sentences that have been picked by the summarizer
L00228:     reference_sentences: The sentences from the referene set
L00229: 
L00230:   Returns:
L00231:     A float: F_lcs
L00232: 
L00233:   Raises:

L00235:   """
L00236:   if len(evaluated_sentences) <= 0 or len(reference_sentences) <= 0:

L00238:   reference_words = _split_into_words(reference_sentences)

L00240:   m = len(reference_words)
L00241:   n = len(evaluated_words)

L00246: def _union_lcs(evaluated_sentences, reference_sentence):

L00249:   subsequence between reference sentence ri and candidate summary C. For example

L00254:   LCS_u(r_i, C) = 4/5.

L00259:
